subject: physics_2
question_text: What happens to the force between two charges if the distance between them is (a) halved (b) doubled?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: F ∝ 1/d², so d → d/2 gives 4F and d → 2d gives F/4 — matches the book (printed p.19).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The inverse square relation
lines: By Coulomb's law, the force between two
charges varies as the inverse square of
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both cases follow from this one proportionality — write it before the cases.
steps.why: Both parts of the question are the same relation read twice. Writing F ∝ 1/d² first turns each case into one line of substitution.
common_mistakes: Using F ∝ 1/d instead of 1/d². The square is the whole point of the law.
Recomputing Coulomb's constant — the charges are unchanged, so only the distance factor matters.

recall.must_convey: That the force varies as the inverse square of the distance, F ∝ 1/d².
accept: F proportional to one by d squared

steps.memory_tip: Distance changes k times → force changes 1/k² times. Everything follows from this.

lines: a) When the distance is halved,

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show the substitution for each case, then state the factor in words.
steps.why: Halving d makes d² four times smaller, so the force is four times larger; doubling d makes d² four times larger, so the force is four times smaller. The two cases are mirror images.
common_mistakes: Answering doubled and halved for the force — the change is by a factor of FOUR, not two.
Swapping the cases: closer means stronger, so halved gives 4F, not F/4.

recall.must_convey: That halving the distance makes the force four times, and doubling it makes the force one fourth.
accept: halved gives four times the force

steps.memory_tip: Closer is stronger: half the distance, four times the force — and the exact mirror when doubled.

insider_note: The factor is four in both cases — an answer of twice or half shows the square was skipped and loses the second mark.
